name: (2019 QC4)
assessment: Traveling at over 47,000 km/h, this 120-meter rock is a brisk but distant visitor to our orbital neighborhood. Its massive miss distance of 19 million kilometers ensures we can sleep soundly while it cruises safely by.

name: (2016 RT17)
assessment: With a modest diameter of 117 meters, this asteroid is moving at a relatively slow pace compared to its peers today. At 26 million kilometers away, it represents a completely harmless curiosity for our deep-space sensors.

name: (2007 DK8)
assessment: This behemoth spans nearly a kilometer and is screaming through the void at a blistering 83,613 km/h. While its size is impressive, its distance of 47 million kilometers means it is essentially a ghost passing in the night.
